meta.name: Sigil Core — Provenance
meta.author: NOMARJ <hello@sigilsec.ai>
meta.description: Detects provenance issues: hidden files, binary files in unexpected locations, suspicious filenames, and large files

provenance_rules.remediation: A hidden file in a package is unusual; check what it does. Editor and VCS dotfiles are excluded already.
Binaries cannot be reviewed as source. Confirm why the package ships one and where it came from.
The filename says what the file is for. Review it before anything else in the package.
Large files are rarely source. Confirm what it is (model weights, a vendored binary, an archive).

provenance_rules.description: Publish hygiene — JavaScript source map shipped in the package
provenance_rules.remediation: Source maps carry the original, unminified source. Exclude *.map from the published artifact (files allowlist in package.json, or .npmignore). This is how 512K lines of Claude Code internals leaked via npm in 2026.

provenance_rules.description: Publish hygiene — CSS source map shipped in the package
Publish hygiene — environment file shipped in the package
provenance_rules.remediation: A committed .env almost always contains real secrets. Remove it, rotate anything in it, and add .env* to .gitignore and .npmignore. (.env.example and .env.template are deliberately not flagged.)

provenance_rules.description: Publish hygiene — private key or keystore file shipped in the package
provenance_rules.remediation: Private key material must never be distributed. Remove the file and rotate the key.

provenance_rules.description: Publish hygiene — PEM file shipped in the package
provenance_rules.remediation: A .pem may be a public CA bundle or a private key. Check its contents; the Credentials phase flags PRIVATE KEY blocks separately.

provenance_rules.description: Publish hygiene — package-manager configuration shipped in the package
provenance_rules.remediation: These files often carry registry tokens. Exclude them from the artifact; the Credentials phase flags any _authToken line.

provenance_rules.description: Publish hygiene — memory or core dump shipped in the package
provenance_rules.remediation: Memory dumps can contain secrets and session data. Remove them.
